clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying an apple orchard: within the year, June grew homesick and wrote to her sister Edna every day, Walter spent long hours in the trees and kept his distance from June, Glen got into fights at his new school and was sent home twice, Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter, and Walter and June had rows over money for new trees. By September 1953, when June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, the household had begun to settle. The shifts across these months show the family's struggle with the move and its aftermath.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: within months, Walter drank heavily most nights, he and Glen blamed each other for the loan, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks grew worse that winter, you began wetting the bed again in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working at the bakery, and by October 1969 Walter had stopped drinking and taken work pruning other men's trees. The shifts pile up around the loss of the orchard and the move to Ridgeport, and the family began to settle once Walter found new work.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: within the year, Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck in the yard for hours, he and Marian had loud fights over money at night, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and said little to your mother, Walter drank again after six years off it, and by June 1976 you were eating again and made the track team. The shifts show the household's response to Glen's loss of work and the strain it put on the marriage and children.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into your house in January 1990 after selling her farm: within months, you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows while Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice, Wilma took over Lily's care, you developed eczema on both hands, you and Hollis had rows most nights, and your mother drove over twice a week to take your side. By June 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town, and by August when your eczema cleared, the household had settled into a new arrangement. The shifts show the family's reaction to Wilma's arrival and the tension it created between you and Hollis.
